items.originalTitle: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
items.author: Siya Tsewu
items.title: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
items.summary: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 15:58 Photo by Salvatore Laporta/KONTROLAB /LightRocket via Getty Images Photo by Salvatore Laporta/KONTROLAB /LightRocket via Getty Images ESHOWE – A police constable allegedly shot and killed three women and injured a man before turning the gun on himself at a tavern in KwaMsane, KwaZulu-Natal. Police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said police responded to reports of a shooting at a liquor establishment at Nkodibe area in KwaMsane, and when they arrived they found four bodies with gunshot wounds, and one victim with a gunshot wound who was taken to hospital. “It was reported that the off-duty police constable also disarmed another man of his firearm during the incident. Both firearms were found at the scene. The cause of the shooting is unknown at this stage.” In a separate incident, police in Eshowe are tracing a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a grocery chain store in Eshowe on Saturday. “Reports indicate that the suspect, who is former employee of the store, had gone to the store for his internal disciplinary hearing. The suspect allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people who were declared dead at the scene. A manhunt for the suspect is underway.”

items.originalTitle: Sold-out MTN8 Final draws thousands to Moses Mabhida Stadium
items.author: Sibonelo Zwane
items.title: Sold-out MTN8 Final draws thousands to Moses Mabhida Stadium
items.summary: Football fever is building up in Durban, where thousands of fans are descending on Moses Mabhida Stadium for tonight’s sold-out MTN8 final. Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns kick off at 6:00 pm, with the Buccaneers chasing a historic fifth consecutive MTN8 crown, while Sundowns are looking to reclaim the trophy they last won in 2021. Orlando Pirates midfielder Thalente Mbatha has shared his recovery journey ahead of the MTN8 Final against Mamelodi Sundowns in Durban. 17:00 SABC 1 Stream on https://t.co/afggCu7f58 #SABCSportFootball #MTN8 https://t.co/2yyNvt3zEa — SABC Sport (@SABC_Sport) October 10, 2026 Supporters are arriving early, with calm returning to the CBD ahead of one of the biggest showdowns on the South African football calendar. “We are here so early because we need to buy tickets and find our seats so we don’t have trouble in traffic when many people are coming into the stadium. We arrived today at 4 am, but we left Mpumalanga last night. I would have felt very sad if protests disrupted the game today because it’s my first ever coming to watch my favourite team play”, says one supporter.

items.originalTitle: ActionSA focuses on drug abuse in Mpumalanga election campaign
items.author: Sibonelo Zwane
items.title: ActionSA focuses on drug abuse in Mpumalanga election campaign
items.summary: With just 25 days to go before the 2026 local government elections, ActionSA in Mpumalanga has focused its campaign on addressing drug abuse in Emalahleni. The party’s eNkangala District mayoral candidate, Mary Phadi, Ekurhuleni mayoral candidate Xolani Khumalo and Johannesburg MMC candidate Zandile Dabula are leading a peaceful walk to raise awareness about drug abuse. IN PICTURES | ActionSA has embarked on a peaceful walk against drug abuse in Emalahleni as part of its election campaign for the 2026 Local Government Elections. The party says drugs are destroying communities and calls for more police on the streets and more rehabilitation centres for addicts. For more, visit https://t.co/LM0zXWIybT Credit: Nhlamulo Mabasa — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 10, 2026 Khumalo says there is a need to reclaim and expropriate hijacked buildings in order to reduce high crime rates. “You see the things that are happening in Jericho; those hijacked buildings are resulting in high crime numbers. They contribute a lot to issues that have to do with prostitution. Therefore, we need law enforcement to do their job; we need law enforcement that works for the district and municipality, not only focusing on by-laws, but also preventing crime; that’s what government needs to do. We know that when ActionSA takes administration, those are the things that will be prioritised. The high rate of unemployment is also a major concern. Our people don’t work; they don’t have job opportunities, and there is no political will to create opportunities for people to find employment. People from Emalahleni don’t work here either; the contractors who supply the mine also need attention.” Meanwhile, Phadi says they hope the walk will have a meaningful impact. “We are saying, let us fix it. We are sending a message to say today we are having a walk, and tomorrow we will not be negotiating with you because our children are drowning in drugs; our children cannot be able to recover for themselves. So, now we are sending a message to those who are illegally selling those drugs. To those who are killing our children, we say now it is time, and you need to move away because when we come as a municipality, you are not going to stand for us.” IN PICTURES | ActionSA has embarked on a peaceful walk against drug abuse in Emalahleni as part of its election campaign for the 2026 Local Government Elections. The party says drugs are destroying communities and calls for more police on the streets and more rehabilitation centres for addicts. For more, visit https://t.co/LM0zXWIybT Credit: Nhlamulo Mabasa — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 10, 2026

items.originalTitle: All Blacks retain Bledisloe Cup with 54-test unbeaten
items.author: Sibonelo Zwane
items.title: All Blacks retain Bledisloe Cup with 54-test unbeaten
items.summary: New Zealand have retained the Bledisloe Cup and have stretched their unbeaten run in tests at Eden Park in Auckland to 54 matches. The All Blacks beat Australia in the first of two tests 50-19, outscoring the Wallabies by seven tries to three. The hosts held a slender 17-14 lead at halftime, but took control of the match in the second half, denying the Wallabies possession and forcing defensive errors. It was also the All Blacks’ 12th consecutive victory over their Trans-Tasman rivals. The second test of the series will be played in Sydney next weekend.

items.originalTitle: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
items.author: Siya Tsewu
items.title: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
items.summary: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 14:47 CAPE TOWN - Ex-Pollsmoor Correctional Centre inmates are using visual art to depict the realities of life behind bars. This they say helps them deal with past trauma, their reintegration into society, and also to make a living. Dubbed "Captured", the visual storytelling project, is set to eventually become a coffee table book. Life behind bars is often reduced to statistics, without the human factor. Enrico Samuels, an artist, served sixteen years behind bars for armed robbery said art connected him with people helping him to navigate life now as a free man. "I want to become a successful artist, doctor is helping me to get there with the projects...lovely projects and I enjoy myself in the projects and from there I see a brighter future from doc's side, because she is taking me that way, so I can see the sun on the other side already,” said Samuels. Michael Sauls said art serves as a conduit in helping them deal with their past and educate the public. “People have no an idea of what prison is like, they think that everything is happy go-lucky or it's like a journey to another paradise, it's not worth it being there...you see it's easy to commit a crime, but it's not easy serving the time." Dr Suzette Leal, the founder of Words Set Free, said the art tells the stories of the people behind it. "If you say the work is beautiful, that's a complement to our artists and their ability, but the story is not beautiful. It's real and true and painful and traumatic. So, I think if anything I hope it discourages someone from getting involved in crime, but I think we don't reduce crime by making prison sentences longer or by making the conditions within them worse. We reduce crime by creating opportunities for people to create a livelihood outside of crime.” Another artist, Kleinbooi Hendricks said: "I said to myself, although the parole board gave me a date to go out of prison, I'm not going. I will either complete my entire sentence but I'm not going out if I haven't worked on myself being a changed man or a different person. I did that because I said I'd either eat out of a dustbin outside, but I'm not going to commit crime again."

items.originalTitle: AU, De Bruyn Foundation congratulate Navi Pillay on Nobel Peace Prize
items.author: Buhle Sibanyoni
items.title: AU, De Bruyn Foundation congratulate Navi Pillay on Nobel Peace Prize
items.summary: The African Union (AU) has congratulated South African jurist Navi Pillay on winning the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, recognising her contributions to international justice, human rights and peace through international law. Pillay oversaw a United Nations report which concluded that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza. African Union Commission Chairperson, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, says Pillay’s career is an enduring legacy for Africa and the world. Pillay fought against apartheid and later served at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, the International Criminal Court and the United Nations. Youssouf says her achievement is a source of pride for African women and girls, and an inspiration to future generations. Similarly, the De Bruyn Foundation has also congratulated Pillay on receiving the Nobel Peace Prize. It joins those celebrating her achievements and her commitment to advancing justice and equality. items.originalTitle: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
items.author: Siya Tsewu
items.title: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
items.summary: Change living conditions – Ndlozi Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 13:42 JOHANNESBURG - Real change begins with communities taking responsibility for their own development. Those are the views of Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, Founder of the Batho Pele Convention. The initiative calls on South Africans to take the lead in improving their own living conditions. “We are here to say you are the solution you are looking for. We are here to say you are the saviour, the developer, the healer and the builder you are looking for. We are here to vote for you to do it on your own. “We are here to say you are the saviours you are looking for. We are not a corporate think tank. Long have we interpreted our misery from broadcast to podcast, think shops to talk shops. “The point is to change our living conditions, one pothole at a time, one classroom at a time and one production hub at a time,” Ndlozi said.

items.originalTitle: Nobel Peace Prize: Trump denounces committee after Navi Pillay win
items.author: Glorious Sefako-Musi
items.title: Nobel Peace Prize: Trump denounces committee after Navi Pillay win
items.summary: United States President Donald Trump has reiterated his complaints about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize. His reaction comes hours after the Nobel Peace Committee awarded the Prize to South African Jurist, Navi Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge. Pillay oversaw a United Nations report which concluded that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza. Trump has expressed disappointment at not winning the prize. “We will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize to the country with the greatest record in history, not 8 wars. We should have had 8 Nobel Prizes for each war, but you didn’t give the Nobel Prize for Peace to the United States of America; it is just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country,” he said. Related video | Navi Pillay describes her Nobel Peace Prize win as “unexpected honour”

items.originalTitle: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
items.author: Siya Tsewu
items.title: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
items.summary: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 12:53 JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg's public pools are missing out on the summer rush. And most are still closed despite the rising temperatures. Community leader Dulton Adams said poor planning, lack of proper budgeting and no clear management plans, are leaving residents without these facilities. The city has 57 public pools , but only 13 are open so far. Ten more are expected to open on Monday. "Every season there's just no budget. There's just no management plan. There's no vision to make sure that the children come off the streets and you look at the pool. This is not the only pool. "Remember spring day, pools must open first. Then the City Council asked for 1 October, pools would be open. That was missed and then now the 7th," Adams said.

items.title: 19 arrested in Durban anti-undocumented immigration protests
items.summary: More than 19 people have been arrested for public violence and malicious damage to property following violent anti-undocumented immigration protests which erupted in Durban over the past two days. Police and security companies are currently patrolling the streets in the CBD after violence and looting on Friday. IMMIGRATION PROTESTS | A South African businesswoman in Durban CBD, who owns a salon and laundry business and employs about 22 people, says she is devastated after her businesses were broken into, looted and set alight. She says several televisions were stolen as tensions continue to escalate in the city centre. — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 9, 2026 A march against undocumented migrants descended into violence after some residents in the Point area threw stones at the marchers. Provincial police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda says they have made several arrests, but it is still early days and they are collecting stats as to how many they’ve arrested. “Because we’ve arrested in different parts of the province, different parts of Durban as well. So at least more than 19 of them, mostly are students, no surprise because saw the numbers on the ground they were young people, most of them. They are arrested for public violence and malicious property damage. We are going to see if there are additional charges for those.” VIDEO | Immigration Crisis | Chaos erupts in Durban

items.originalTitle: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
items.author: Siya Tsewu
items.title: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
items.summary: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 11:22 JOHANNESBURG - The ANC could emerge as the biggest loser in this year's municipal elections. This is the view is political strategist Brutus Malada. He said the party’s declining support could leave it with less influence across key metros and this could push it into a weakened position ahead of the 2029 elections. “ANC will be the big loser in this. The trend is clear. It's clear that they are losing at a margin of 10 to 12 percent and that will actually mean the end of the ANC and it will become lame duck for this period in between the two elections. “That it will sit, it will be a national government President Ramaphosa sitting in Tshwane. The Union Buildings which is led by another party and in Cape Town which is the legislative arm of the state which is led by the DA. “So here is a political party that is running the country as the head of the State but it has no control of the economy hub, it has no control of administrative hub, it has no control of legislative hub,” Malada said.

items.originalTitle: New Zealand’s O’Rourke ruled out of India series
items.author: Buhle Sibanyoni
items.title: New Zealand’s O’Rourke ruled out of India series
items.summary: New Zealand fast-bowler Will O’Rourke will miss the series against India as he continues his rehabilitation from injuries to his left hamstring and calf, the country’s cricket board said on Saturday. O’Rourke suffered a hamstring tear during New Zealand’s test series win over England in June, before hurting his calf in training in late August. The 25-year-old will aim to return to full fitness ahead of a four-test tour of neighbours Australia beginning on December 9. “It’s obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India,” New Zealand coach Rob Walter said in a statement. “He was set to feature in both the ODI and test series, but following subsequent discussions, we all agreed it was best for him to take some more time to rehabilitate both injuries and safely build up his bowling loads. “Our pace bowling resources will be critical over the next few months so we’re taking a conservative approach to Will’s return to ensure he’s fully fit before he takes the field again.” New Zealand host India in five Twenty20 internationals, five one-day internationals and two tests, with the opening T20 in Christ church on October 22.

items.originalTitle: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi
items.author: Siya Tsewu
items.title: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi
items.summary: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 11:15 Mamelodi – The family and friends of the slain 14-year-old twins have gathered in Mamelodi West to bid farewell to the boys. Bonolo and Botlhale Makena were found dead in their home a week ago. They had multiple stab wounds. The boys' mother made the gruesome discovery at home, when she returned from work. As police investigate, residents are demanding that this case does not become another unresolved killing. Neighobour Padi Matlala said the Mamelodi West community is demanding justice. “The community has been here before. The community is saying, ‘please justice system, don't take us there.’ We were there in 1982. Two members of the community were brutally murdered. 44 years later, nobody has been held responsible. “The community is saying justice system never, never again should you go through this. The pressure that you put on the government throughout the week, the outrage you showed must bear fruit. Somebody or some people must be held responsible for this. We are better than this,” Matlala said.

items.originalTitle: Wheelchair-bound man dies in shack fire in Katlehong
items.author: Sibonelo Zwane
items.title: Wheelchair-bound man dies in shack fire in Katlehong
items.summary: A 38-year-old man who was wheelchair bound, has died in a shack fire in Zonkizizwe Extension Six in Katlehong in Ekurhuleni. Firefighters responded to the blaze on Friday night, but the man was found deceased beneath the collapsed corrugated iron sheets after the fire was extinguished. Ekurhuleni Disaster and Emergency Management Service (EMS) spokesperson William Ntladi says investigations are underway to determine the cause of the fire. “On arrival, members of the community were found busy with a bucket brigade system, desperately extinguishing the blaze. Firefighters used attack lines from the fire engine and successfully managed to bring the blaze under control, desperately striving to rescue a wheelchair-bound man who was reported to be still trapped inside the shack. During the search, rescue and recovery after the blaze was extinguished, the man’s burnt body was found under the corrugated metal sheets. Paramedics attended to him, and he was declared dead on scene. The scene was officially handed over to the South African Police Service officers.”

items.summary: Students arrested at Durban protest Siya Tsewu Sat, 10/10/2026 - 10:28 DURBAN - Over 19 people have been arrested during violent protests in Durban last night. The city has been on fire this week, with shops looted, vehicles torched and property destroyed. KZN Premier Thami Ntuli wants army deployment to quell the ant-illegal migrant protests, against the processing of asylum seekers. Demonstrations continued last night despite government's withdrawal of the directive. KZN Police Spokesperson Robert Netshiunda confirmed the arrests. “We can tell you that over 19 people were arrested and most of them are students. They have been charged with public violence,” Netshiunda said.

items.title: Some Durban protesters say unaware of withdrawn asylum directive
items.summary: Some protesters in Durban say they were unaware that the Department of Home Affairs had withdrawn a directive expanding access to asylum application processes following a Constitutional Court ruling. The ruling has become a subject of debate as tensions escalate, with anti-immigration protesters engaging in violent demonstrations across the city. Several buildings have been damaged, shops looted and vehicles set alight as protesters demand that the government address their concerns about immigration. Police have increased their presence in an effort to contain the violence, as unrest continues to spread across Durban. Immigration Crisis | Chaos erupts in Durban: These protesters share their views about the Home Affairs stance. “I was not aware that Home Affairs had decided to withdraw. I’ve been here at this march since very early this morning, so I have not been checking any updates on social media or on the news. However, as much as I am happy with this move by Home Affairs, I still think we need to continue with this march; we have had enough,” says a protester. “I was also not aware. I think we can continue protesting, but, however, it needs to be done in a peaceful manner. No one must be harmed; property must not be destroyed,” says another protester. items.originalTitle: Three civilians injured as suspected CIT robbers crash on N12
items.author: Zandile.Khumalo
items.title: Three civilians injured as suspected CIT robbers crash on N12

It is the second consecutive day of violence in the Durban city centre. Ntuli says law enforcement agencies have been reinforced but with the violence intensifying, he believes the deployment of the army is necessary to restore law and order. “In fact, I have already spoken to the Police Minister to say the situation one runs that the army is deployed in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. Ntuli says they also engage protest leaders. “Well, we will engage the leaders that are involved, but at the same time, more police are being deployed in the province. Some are arriving from outside to assist. That is what we have underground, and we are activating. Even yesterday, they were part of those who were forced multipliers to ensure that we calmed the situation,” says Ntuli. Immigration Crisis | KZN Premier requests SANDF deployment: Ntuli has also raised concerns over investor confidence following violent protests in the Durban CBD for the last two days. Ntuli warned that continuous protest action signal instability, threatening crucial foreign investment and job creation across the province. “We are having a conference in KwaZulu-Natal on the 15 th , and I’m worried that when this is happening, the confidence of investors is affected adversely. Hence, I’m calling for the people of KwaZulu-Natal to join hands with us and say no one must destroy, no one must loot in the name of the people who are having genuine concerns,” adds Ntuli. items.originalTitle: FCC chief defers to Pentagon on airing US execution on TV networks
items.author: Preggie Moodley
items.title: FCC chief defers to Pentagon on airing US execution on TV networks
items.summary: The chair of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Friday that he would defer to the Pentagon on whether US networks could air a planned December 3 military execution , which would be an unprecedented broadcast . US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others at the Fort Hood military base in Texas in 2009, would be livestreamed. Carr told CNBC it was his understanding this would not air on broadcast TV. But asked if he would allow it to be aired, he said: “Ultimately we’re going to defer to Secretary Hegseth and you know his decisions on how to move forward with this.” A n FCC spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ABC, NBC, CBS and Fox did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether they are considering airing the execution. Andrew Jay Schwartzman, a senior counselor at the Benton Institute for Broadband & Society and expert on FCC issues, said there is no legal basis for the commission to intervene in a broadcaster’s decision on whether to air a live execution. “There is absolutely no justification in the Communications Act or the Constitution that would allow the FCC to tell broadcasters to carry or not carry an actual event,” he said, adding, “there is no basis for the FCC to dictate content or to prohibit content short of obscenity.” A 2007 report from the FCC on violence on television said the agency did not have the authority to regulate violent content. The report said “violent speech and depictions of violence have been found by the courts to be protected by the First Amendment.”

items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has condemned newly announced United States sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) as an institution, warning they threaten its ability to deliver justice for victims of international crimes. He called the decision a serious blow to international criminal justice. His statement follows Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay ‘s warning to SABC News that independent courts were under attack. The SG’s Spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said Guterres was calling upon all states to uphold their commitments under international law, and to support efforts aimed at ensuring accountability for the most serious crimes of concern to the international community. UN human rights chief Volker Turk on Friday called for immediate measures to protect the International Criminal Court (ICC) after the United States imposed “unacceptable” sanctions upon it. “These sanctions – the latest in a series of retaliatory steps against the ICC and its personnel for the work they do every day to advance accountability for the very worst violations of human rights – are unacceptable,” Turk said. EU countries including host country the Netherlands will take measures to keep the ICC functioning after the United States impose sanctions on it, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and EU Council President Antonio Costa said at a joint press conference on Friday. Jetten said it was “crucial” that there is still time to continue talks with the US during the six-month period before the sanctions take effect. – additional report by Reuters

items.originalTitle: Australia fight back in a first test before bad light ends play
items.author: Thabiso Malesele
items.title: Australia fight back in a first test before bad light ends play
items.summary: Australia’s captain Pat Cummins and Matt Renshaw led an afternoon fightback to see the tourists to 187-6 before bad light brought a premature halt to play on the opening day of the first test against South Africa on Friday. The pair put on an unbeaten 63 for the seventh wicket with Renshaw four runs short of a fifty and Cummins 33 not out. The umpires took the players off one hour before the scheduled close as windy and gloomy conditions coincided with South Africa bringing back the pacy Anrich Nortje into the attack and when he sent a bouncer over Renshaw’s head, play was immediately halted after the light meters were consulted. The umpires waited out in the middle for another 45 minutes before calling off the day’s proceedings. Nortje was returning after almost four years away from first-class cricket, and took two wickets in the space of three balls before tea to give the hosts the upper hand. The 32-year-old had not played since March 2023 as persistent injury and a focus on the T20 format kept him away from red-ball cricket but he justified his recall with a fiery spell after lunch that left the tourists teetering. Nortje brings x-factor South Africa captain Temba Bavuma predicted Nortje could provide X-factor, and he did as much in having Alex Carey caught at second slip off a fuller delivery that clocked in at 143 kph and then, two balls later, snagging Beau Webster caught behind to see Australia fall to 124-6. “To be honest I thought I wasn’t going to get a wicket for the next few weeks the way the ball was passing the bat but then it was good to take the wickets and get the blood flowing again,” Nortje said at the post-match press conference. The fortunes of Nortje, who finished the day with 2-40 off 13.2 overs, contrasted with those of Australian cancer survivor Nic Maddinson, also making a comeback, who failed to get a run. The 34-year-old, a surprise choice to open after Australia won the toss and chose to bat, survived 33 balls without scoring before Marco Jansen bowled him to end a remarkable return following his battle with cancer last year. His duck was the longest by an Australian opener in test history and the third-longest by any test opener. It was Maddinson’s first test appearance in almost a decade, having not played first-class cricket for 18 months as he fought testicular cancer that had spread to his lungs. He was only named in the team half an hour before play started Australia counter-attacked after Travis Head (9) and Maddinson went early, with Marnus Labuschagne and Steve Smith putting together a 60-run partnership for the third wicket before Wiaan Mulder (2-31) trapped Labuschagne lbw for 37 with the last ball before lunch. Smith’s first test in South Africa after sandpapergate Smith scored 25 on his first test appearance in South Africa since the 2018 tour that led to his one-year ban for his role in the ball-tampering scandal known as “Sandpapergate”. Smith walked to the crease without any noticeable heckling from the sparse crowd and quickly set about speeding up the scoring, with two sixes when spinner Keshav Maharaj was introduced to the home attack. However, Smith was dismissed in the first over after lunch, getting a thick edge to gully to earn Jansen (2-35) a second wicket. Renshaw said South Africa had bowled tight and there were many challenges for the visiting batsmen to face. “Some pace, some bounces, some nibble, some spin, but I think there were moments in the game where I felt like we were getting close to having the foot on their throat.”

items.originalTitle: Youth urged to vote in 4 November LGE
items.author: Preggie Moodley
items.title: Youth urged to vote in 4 November LGE
items.summary: The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) and the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) hosted a mock voting station at the SABC on Friday to demonstrate the voting process ahead of the 4 November 2026 Local Government Elections. The demonstration took participants through the voting process, from joining the queue to casting their ballots. Depending on where they live, voters will receive different ballot papers. These include: • Ward ballot: Voters choose a candidate to represent their ward. • Proportional Representation (PR) ballot: Voters choose a political party, with council seats allocated according to each party’s share of the vote. • District council ballot: Voters choose a political party to represent them on the district council. Voters in metropolitan municipalities receive two ballot papers: a ward ballot and a PR ballot. Voters in local municipalities outside metropolitan areas receive three, including a district council ballot. IEC regional outreach officer Diana Mola said the commission runs educational programmes to encourage young people to participate in elections, from primary school through to tertiary education. “When we go to high schools, secondary schools, that’s where we get the people who are qualified to register. In our laws, to register, you need to be 16 years,” she said. Mola encouraged young people to consider standing for leadership positions, saying they could participate in elections as candidates as well as voters. “You don’t only engage with the voting by becoming a voter. You can even become a candidate, as long as you are a South African citizen and you are a registered voter,” she said. According to the IEC, 42.1% of people aged between 18 and 35 are registered to vote, while about 22.65% of candidates contesting the elections fall within the same age group. Meanwhile, SABC specialist researcher Velemseni Mthiyane encouraged young people to exercise their democratic right and participate in the elections. “The youth must remember that their voice will always make a difference, whether or not they are able to see the tangible results,” he said.
